catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is usually predictable. It occurs on the second syllable in words that do not contain the consonants / ɣ β r / . Syllables that begin with these sounds are weak and do not count as syllables when placing the stress.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is verbatim on p. 3 of the held Lee 1994 OPD (page image read; text layer loses ɣ β only). (2) Deciding source is a primary SIL phonology datasheet by the long-term fieldworker; short, hedged ('usually'), no examples, but first-hand. Against Glottolog (13 refs, none phonological besides syntax sketches and Bible materials) and the SIL archive listing (8 entries, the only unseen descriptive items being a 1978 83-pp grammar-essentials ms, a 1984 draft dictionary and a 7-pp word-classes note, none online), nothing better on Madak stress is known to exist; Wikipedia's statement derives from the same OPD. (3) list of works to obtain is the 1978 grammar essentials (medium) and the 1984 dictionary (low), both print/archive-only.
